name: AdPriva
author: AdPriva

sections.description:
AdPriva verifies your traffic with cryptographic proofs so you can see which visits the
automation checks flagged. Install the plugin, click Connect with AdPriva (a secure OAuth sign-in — no API keys
to copy), and the plugin will:

  • Register and verify your site with AdPriva automatically.
  • Provision a site placement and load the AdPriva verification tag on your site from the AdPriva CDN.
  • Show a traffic & validity summary right on your WordPress dashboard, with a link to your full
    AdPriva console.

The plugin is self-sufficient inside wp-admin:

  • Settings page — control where the tag loads (post types, exclude logged-in users,
    administrators, or specific URLs), choose whether the tag waits for visitor consent (consent
    mode), toggle the dashboard widget, and (advanced) override the AdPriva endpoints. Consent
    plugins can suppress the tag through the adpriva_should_load_tag filter.
  • In-admin dashboard — KPI cards, a check-results breakdown, and a trend chart over the
    last 7, 30, or 90 days, all without leaving WordPress.

No personal data about your visitors is collected by this plugin. Verification happens server-side at
AdPriva using privacy-preserving signals.

Connecting

After activating, open the AdPriva menu in wp-admin and click Connect with AdPriva. You will be
sent to AdPriva to approve the connection for your organization, then returned to your site — connected.

External services

This plugin connects to AdPriva, a third-party service, to verify your traffic. This is required for
the plugin to function.

1. AdPriva API — https://api.adpriva.com
Used to: complete the “Connect with AdPriva” sign-in (OAuth 2.0 authorization-code with PKCE), register
and verify your site’s domain, provision a site placement, and fetch your traffic summary and per-day
trend for the dashboard widget and the in-admin dashboard.
Data sent: your site’s domain, the OAuth authorization parameters, and the access token issued to this
install. No visitor personal data is sent by the plugin.
Terms: https://adpriva.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://adpriva.com/privacy

2. AdPriva verification tag (CDN) — https://cdn.adpriva.com/tag.js
Used to: load the lightweight verification tag on your site’s front end so AdPriva can verify
traffic. The tag identifies your site by its domain. The script is served from AdPriva’s CDN and
loads asynchronously. Before 1.3.0 the plugin loaded it from https://cdn.adpriva-ads.com/tag.js,
which serves the same file and stays available (Settings → Advanced → Tag script URL).
Terms: https://adpriva.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://adpriva.com/privacy

3. AdPriva ingest server — https://ingest.adpriva.com
Used by the tag (in your visitors’ browsers, not by the plugin) to send one page-view event per page
load. A tag loaded from the legacy https://cdn.adpriva-ads.com/tag.js sends to
https://server.adpriva-ads.com instead, the same service under its old name. Data sent: aggregate interaction counts, automation hints, a low-detail device snapshot (screen
and window size, platform, colour depth), the page path and the referrer. Like any web request, it
also reaches the server with the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent. With the consent mode
set to Manual (the default), Didomi or TCF, the tag sends nothing until the visitor consents.
Terms: https://adpriva.com/terms — Privacy Policy: https://adpriva.com/privacy

Privacy

  • The plugin stores a single option in your database holding the AdPriva connection: access/refresh
    tokens (encrypted at rest using your site’s WordPress salts), your placement ID, and your domain.
  • The plugin does not set cookies and does not collect or store your visitors’ personal data.
  • You can disconnect at any time from the AdPriva settings page; this revokes the access token and
    deletes the stored connection. Uninstalling the plugin removes all stored data.
  • Respecting consent: the tag only loads when connected and when your Settings → Tag targeting rules
    allow it, and a consent/privacy plugin can always suppress it via the adpriva_should_load_tag
    filter (the filter is the final override).
  • Consent mode (Settings → Visitor consent): with Manual (the default) the tag waits until your
    site calls AdPriva.grantConsent(); with Didomi it waits for consent to an AdPriva custom
    vendor and purpose in Didomi; with TCF it waits for purpose 1 in your IAB TCF v2 consent banner.
    In these modes it sends nothing before consent and stops when consent is withdrawn. Off
    starts the tag at page load and needs a confirmation when you choose it. The plugin prints the chosen mode on the tag’s script in every mode,
    Off included, so it always wins over a consent preset set elsewhere on the page.
  • Settings are stored in a separate adpriva_settings option; they contain no visitor data.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/adpriva, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open the AdPriva menu and click Connect with AdPriva.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AdPriva account?

Yes. The Connect button signs you in to AdPriva; you approve the connection for your organization.

Does this collect my visitors’ personal data?

No. The plugin sends your site’s domain and the connection token to AdPriva. Traffic verification is
performed by AdPriva using privacy-preserving signals.

How do I stop loading the tag?

Disconnect from the AdPriva settings page, or use the adpriva_should_load_tag filter to control it.

Can the tag wait for my visitors’ consent?

Yes. Under Settings → Visitor consent, choose Manual (the default) to call
AdPriva.grantConsent() and AdPriva.revokeConsent() from your own consent tool, Didomi if you use
Didomi and have added AdPriva as a custom vendor and purpose, or TCF if your consent banner supports
the IAB TCF v2 framework (the tag then waits for consent to purpose 1, “Store and/or access information
on a device”; this is not AdPriva vendor consent). Setup steps for Cookiebot, OneTrust, Usercentrics and Google Tag Manager are at
https://docs.adpriva.com/developer-docs/tag-installation/#consent-modes
sections.changelog:
1.3.2

  • Changed: the consent mode now defaults to Manual. A new install collects nothing until your site calls AdPriva.grantConsent(), and a missing or unknown value is treated as Manual, never as Off.
  • New: a Didomi consent mode, with the custom vendor ID and purpose IDs from your Didomi Console. The placeholder purpose ID is rejected.
  • Changed: choosing Off (collect on page load) needs a confirmation checkbox. The TCF help text now says plainly that it checks purpose 1, not AdPriva vendor consent.
  • Upgrade: a connected site that never saved the consent mode keeps Off, now stored explicitly, and shows a notice recommending Manual, TCF or Didomi.

1.3.1

  • Changed: the dashboard and the dashboard widget now use the check-result names the AdPriva console uses: “No automation found”, “AI agent”, “Automation detected” and “Some checks failed”, under the heading “Check results”. The checks show which automation rules fired; they cannot show that a person was there, so “Human” and “Abusive bots” are gone. The numbers are unchanged.
  • Translations: regenerated the .pot file.

1.3.0

  • Changed: the tag now loads from https://cdn.adpriva.com/tag.js and sends to https://ingest.adpriva.com. The previous hosts, cdn.adpriva-ads.com and server.adpriva-ads.com, serve the same tag and stay available: set Settings → Advanced → Tag script URL to https://cdn.adpriva-ads.com/tag.js to keep them.
  • Changed: with the consent mode set to Off, the tag’s <script> now carries data-consent-mode="off". Off always wins, also over a window.AdPriva.consentMode set by your theme or another plugin, and your site keeps its behaviour if the tag’s default for a missing mode ever changes.

1.2.0

  • New: Settings → Visitor consent → Consent mode. TCF makes the tag wait for consent from your IAB TCF v2 consent banner; Manual makes it wait until your site calls AdPriva.grantConsent(). In both modes the tag sends nothing before consent and stops when consent is withdrawn. Off, the default, keeps the current behaviour. This is a new setting, unrelated to the “Consent integration” option removed in 1.1.0.
  • Changed: the tag’s <script> now loads with async, so it never delays your pages.
  • Translations: added the new strings to the .pot file.

1.1.0

  • Removed: the “Consent integration” setting. It never changed when the tag loads. To hold the tag until consent, use the adpriva_should_load_tag filter (unchanged).
  • Removed: the data-placement attribute on the tag’s <script> and the “Placement ID” line on the Settings page. The tag identifies your site by its domain and never read the attribute.
  • Translations: regenerated the .pot file.

1.0.2

  • Fixed: the default AdPriva console address now points at console.adpriva.com. The “Open console” links in the dashboard, settings page, and widget previously went to the wrong AdPriva app unless you had set an endpoint override.

1.0.1

  • Compliance: the Contributors field now lists the plugin owner’s WordPress.org account, as required for the directory listing.
  • Removed the unused Plugin URI header and hardened WordPress Plugin Check (strict mode) for a clean review. No functional changes.

1.0.0

  • First stable release, submitted to the WordPress.org plugin directory.
  • Connect with AdPriva via OAuth 2.0 authorization-code with PKCE — no API keys to copy.
  • Loads the AdPriva verification tag from the CDN with your provisioned placement ID.
  • Settings page: tag targeting (post types, exclude logged-in users / administrators / URLs), consent integration mode, dashboard preferences, and advanced endpoint overrides.
  • In-admin dashboard and dashboard widget: KPI cards, check-results breakdown, and a 7/30/90-day trend chart.

0.2.0

  • New: in-admin dashboard with KPI cards, verdict breakdown, and a 7/30/90-day trend chart (no console trip needed).
  • New: Settings page — tag targeting (post types, exclude logged-in users / administrators / URLs), consent integration mode, dashboard preferences, and advanced endpoint overrides.
  • New: the dashboard widget can be toggled from Settings, and now links to the in-admin dashboard.
  • Endpoint URLs resolve as: a wp-config constant wins, then a Settings override, then the built-in default.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: Connect with AdPriva (OAuth + PKCE), CDN tag injection, and a dashboard traffic widget.

upgrade_notice.1.3.2: New installs now default to the Manual consent mode, and there is a new Didomi mode. A site that is already connected keeps its current behaviour (Off) and shows a notice recommending a consent mode.
upgrade_notice.1.3.1: Wording only: the dashboard now uses the console's check-result names instead of "Human" and "Abusive bots". No settings or data change.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: The tag moves to cdn.adpriva.com and sends to ingest.adpriva.com. If your site sets a Content Security Policy, allow both, or set Tag script URL to https://cdn.adpriva-ads.com/tag.js. Off now always wins over a page's own consent preset.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Adds an optional consent mode for the tag (Settings → Visitor consent) and loads the tag asynchronously. The default, Off, changes nothing for your visitors.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Removes the unused "Consent integration" setting and the unused placement attribute on the tag. Your connection and settings are kept.
upgrade_notice.1.0.1: Metadata and directory-compliance fixes only; no functional changes.
upgrade_notice.1.0.0: First stable release of AdPriva for WordPress.
upgrade_notice.0.2.0: Adds an in-admin dashboard and a full Settings page. No action required; your existing connection is preserved.
upgrade_notice.0.1.0: First public release of AdPriva for WordPress.
